classification_rationale: The justifying comment asserted an equivalence the code did not hold.

Supersedes the pass-1 row: fix landed in f259cefb1 and was corrected in f2708a5db after Gate 8 found the marker was stamped unconditionally. Closure evidence is the mutation-checked test pair in tests/unit/server/test_workflow_routes.cpp.

classification_rationale: Real defect in the confinement fix itself: the KPI Total cell falls open to the fleet-wide count whenever an out-of-scope target has not yet reported, which is the normal startup window of every execution, not an edge case.
trigger: Confined operator opens the executions drawer for a dispatch that targeted an out-of-scope agent which has not yet reported a status row.
summary: roster_dropped only observes agents that HAVE reported (agent_exec_status rows are created solely by ExecutionTracker::update_agent_status, never pre-populated at dispatch), so an out-of-scope target that has not yet answered is invisible to filter_rows_in_scope and roster_dropped stays 0 -- the KPI strip then falls through to the unfiltered exec.agents_targeted. Independently found by Codex (Phase 1) and confirmed by Kimi (Phase 2) and FortitudeEtc directly against the source. Fixed in a85179501: Total now recomputes from the reported roster whenever it is incomplete AND the scope machinery is active, not only on an observed drop; the data-scope-reconciled marker widens the same way so the live SSE channel cannot re-disclose the withheld number. New regression test pins the exact scenario (test_workflow_routes.cpp, out-of-scope-target-not-yet-reported section). The full fix -- persisting the target roster so pending status rows exist at dispatch -- remains open per the review's own framing.
